processing_steps.method: casting in a vacuum induction furnace
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The steel was casted using a vacuum induction furnace.

processing_steps.method: hot forging to rods with a section plane of 35 mm × 70 mm × 100 mm
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Followed by air cooling to room temperature.

processing_steps.method: hot rolling to 3 mm thickness steel sheet through 6 passes
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: reduced to 3 mm thickness through 6 passes
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Start rolling temperature 1150 °C and finish rolling temperature 850 °C.

processing_steps.method: water quenching to 550 °C followed by air cooling to room temperature
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The hot-rolled steel was subsequently water quenched to 550 °C, followed by air cooling to room temperature.
Defines the H100 specimen (solution treated at 1000 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching).

structures.overall_structure: After solution treatment at 1000 °C for 1 h (H100), martensite appeared again and only 12.9% austenite was retained. The microstructure consists of blocky δ-ferrite, α-ferrite, austenite and martensite; a dashed-box inset shows the martensite with a lath/needle morphology.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: tensile specimens with a gauge width of 12.5 mm and a gauge length of 50 mm machined from the solution-treated sheets along the longitudinal direction
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Mechanical performance reported in Table 3 for the solution-treated specimens; density measured by densitometry (Archimedes principle); phase hardness from Table 2.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SE-SEM (Signal A = SE2, EHT = 15.00 kV); panel (d) H100 at Mag = 1.07 K X, WD = 8.9 mm, 10 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe and identify the microstructure/phases of the H100 specimen (solution treated at 1000 °C for 1 h)
characterization_methods.key_findings: H100 shows blocky δ-ferrite, α-ferrite, austenite and martensite; an inset reveals lath/needle-shaped martensite; martensite reappeared with only 12.9% austenite retained.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: direct comparison method using integrated intensities of (200)α and (211)α for ferrite and (220)γ and (311)γ for austenite
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the volume fraction of austenite (and the C content in austenite)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Austenite volume fraction of H100 is 12.9% (Table 3).

characterization_methods.purpose: Distinguish the phases present (austenite, δ-ferrite, α-ferrite, martensite) in the solution-treated specimens
characterization_methods.key_findings: Austenite 275 ± 10 HV; δ-ferrite 314 ± 15 HV; α-ferrite 374 ± 10 HV; martensite 438 ± 15 HV.

characterization_methods.purpose: Investigate the element distribution in austenite and ferrite; determine Mn and Al contents of austenite
characterization_methods.key_findings: EDS analysis of element distribution and Mn/Al contents of austenite (Table 4 covers H70–H90).

characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the density of the steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: Density about 6.95 g/cm3, about 11% lower than pure Fe.

analytical_models.model_name: Austenite lattice parameter / C content equation
analytical_models.equation_role: Determines the austenite lattice parameter α_γ (in Å) from C, Mn and Al concentrations (wt%) so that the C content in austenite can be obtained from the (220) d-spacing
analytical_models.model_note: Equation (1): α_γ = 3.578 + 0.0330 X_C + 0.0056 X_Al + 0.00095 X_Mn. Applied to determine C content in austenite (reported for H70–H90 in Table 4; no H100 value reported).

analytical_models.equation_role: Calculates the martensitic transformation starting temperature from alloying element contents (mass%)
analytical_models.model_note: Equation (2). Ms temperatures reported for H70 (33 °C), H80 (67 °C) and H90 (120 °C); no H100 value reported.

analytical_models.equation_role: Calculates the temperature at which 50% of austenite transforms to martensite at a true strain of 30%
analytical_models.model_note: Equation (3). Md30 temperatures reported for H70 (268 °C per text / 168 °C per Table 4), H80 (204 °C) and H90 (249 °C); no H100 value reported.

unmapped_findings: The Ms and Md30 temperatures calculated from Eqs. (2) and (3) are reported only for H70, H80 and H90 (Table 4); no Ms/Md30 value is given for H100.
The EBSD phase-fraction vs strain analysis (Fig. 3), the Schmid factor analysis (Fig. 4) and the fracture/TEM study (Fig. 5) were carried out only on H90, not on H100.
Density of the steel is about 6.95 g/cm3, about 11% lower than pure iron; measured on the steel (applicable to all solution-treated specimens).
Among the four solution-treated specimens, H100 had the highest UTS (860.3 MPa) but the lowest total elongation (15.0%).
Table 1 chemical composition of the investigated alloy (wt%): C 0.15, Mn 7.35, Al 6.00, P < 0.005, S 0.01, Fe balance (designation Fe-8Mn-6Al-0.2C is rounded relative to measured values).
